newsitem.title: UK: Profits soar at N Brown home shopping group.
newsitem.headline: Profits soar at N Brown home shopping group.

text.p: British direct mail order retailer N Brown Group Plc said on Tuesday a marketing drive and wider product ranges propelled annual earnings and sales sharply higher.

The company, which targets older consumers and recently abandoned talks to buy Sears Plc's Freemans home shopping business, said pretax profits rose 19 percent to 37.1 million pounds ($60.1 million) in the year to March 1997. The total dividend rose 19 percent to 6.8 pence.

"It was a remarkable result...if you take into account the previous year's 53-week period and a value-added-tax windfall, then that puts the earnings rise at about 25 percent," chief executive Jim Martin said in a telephone interview.

Martin said it would be difficult to maintain that profit growth, which was driven by a seven percent rise in its established customer base. Broader ranges of womenswear, menswear and furniture and the acquisition of Sartor, a household products and inexpensive clothing retailer, also helped.
"But we had 15 percent sales growth in the first six weeks and that level is certainly possible for the future," Martin said, adding that demographic changes were working in N Brown's favour.
Sales grew 21.5 percent last year to 280.5 million pounds and footwear, household goods and furniture ranges would be expanded this year.
Martin said N Brown was increasingly looking towards older consumers, between 30 and retirement age, who were benefiting from higher savings, better pensions and inheritance windfalls.

"The post-war baby boomers will be coming of age in the late 90s and in early 2000 and there will be a 27 percent increase in the next 10 years in women between 55 and 64," he said, adding that N Brown would also seek to cater for low-income groups.

N Brown said it counted 1.7 million established customers last year who increased their average spend by seven percent. Womenswear sales, which account for more than half of all turnover, rose by 18 percent and menswear turnover was up 38 percent.
Martin said N Brown was maintaining its share --around 25 percent -- of the direct home shopping market in which it competes with Next Plc, among others.
The company has around five percent of the wider home shopping market, which includes agency companies such as Great Universal Stores Plc and Littlewoods LWD.CN, Martin said.

Martin said he was "not too worried" about Littlewoods' bid to buy Freemans. Retail industry sources believes Littlewoods will overcome competition watchdog concerns and take over the Sears' subsidiary, Britain's third-largest mail order company.
"We feel we have our own part of the marketplace and we are quite satisfied with that," he said.

N Brown figures show sales from its midlife catalogue ranges, including J D Williams, Shoe Tailor, Oxendales and Fifty Plus, rose 14 percent last year, accounting for 205 million pounds of total catalogue sales of 274 million.
Sales to the elderly, including the disabled, more than doubled to 17 million pounds. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
